stories.headline: 2024 Lok Sabha polls: DMDK’s Vijaya Prabhakaran to withdraw election petition against Congress MP Manickam Tagore’s victory
stories.title: 2024 Lok Sabha polls: DMDK’s Vijaya Prabhakaran to withdraw election petition against Congress MP Manickam Tagore’s victory
stories.summary: The election petition had accused the then DMK Ministers K.K.S.S.R. Ramachandran, Thangam Thennarasu and P. Moorthy of exerting pressure on the Returning Officer
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Desiya Murpokku Dravida Kazhagam (DMDK) youth wing secretary V. Vijaya Prabhakaran, has decided to withdraw an election petition filed by him before the Madras High Court in 2024 challenging the victory of incumbent Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) president B. Manickam Tagore from Virudhunagar Lok Sabha constituency in the parliamentary elections.

In an application filed before Justice N. Sathish Kumar, Mr. Prabhakaran said he does not want to take the election petition for trial since he had decided to bestow his attention to public life rather than continuing the litigation pending for last two years.
He sought the leave of the court, under Sections 109 and 110 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, to withdraw the election petition.

The judge has directed the applicant to issue notice to all the parties to the election petition besides issuing a publication in the official government gazette expressing his desire to withdraw the election petition to find out if any other eligible person was interested in substituting himself/herself in the place of the election petitioner in order to continue the challenge made to the victory of Virudhunagar MP Mr. Tagore.

Virudhunagar Lok Sabha constituency had witnessed a keenly contested three-cornered fight between Mr. Tagore, Mr. Prabhakaran and actor R. Radikaa Sarathkumar who was fielded as a candidate of Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
Mr. Tagore had polled 3,85,256 votes and defeated his nearest rival Mr. Prabhakaran by a slim margin of 4,379 votes with the latter securing as many as 3,80,877 votes.

In his election petition, Mr. Prabhakaran had accused Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer V.P. Jeyaseelan, who was the Returning Officer of Virudhunagar paliamentary constituency, of having succumbed to the pressure exerted by the then DMK Ministers K.K.S.S.R. Ramachandran, Thangam Thennarasu and P. Moorthy for furthering the prospects of the election of their then alliance party candidate Mr. Tagore.
Mr. Prabhakaran had also raised other grounds such as improper acceptance of nomination paper by claiming the MP had not disclosed all details regarding his assets and criminal cases.
He had further accused the MP of having won the election by indulging in electoral corrupt practices such as bribing the voters through distribution of a ‘guarantee card’ and so on.

Paying cash for votes, booth capturing, malpractices during the counting of votes, improper rejection of postal ballots polled in favour of the election petitioner and alleged excess expenditure by the MP were the other grounds on which his election had been challenged.
Mr. Tagore had taken out an application in 2024 itself to reject the election petition and strike off the allegations levelled against him.
The MP argued the guarantee card contained an assurance given by the Congress in its election manifesto and therefore such an assurance could not be termed as a corrupt practice.

stories.headline: Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi | Dissent in the Election Commission
stories.title: Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi | Dissent in the Election Commission
stories.summary: The two Election Commissioner, both appointed by the government under the new 2023 law, have raised questions about changes to electoral rolls, centralised control and the Election Commission’s decision-making process
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: When notices began to be issued after the publication of the draft list during the Delhi SIR [special intensive revision], one of the names was that of Election Commissioner (EC) Sukhbir Singh Sandhu.

What was considered ironical on that day and time soon became a moment of reckoning for the poll body as reports emerged that Dr. Sandhu, along with his fellow Election Commissioner Vivek Joshi, had flagged many anomalies in the ongoing SIR process across the country over the last 10 months.

Though rumours of a rift within the Election Commission of India had been doing the rounds for some months, what came as a surprise were the formal dissent notes written by the two ECs, including one to the Cabinet Secretary, as both had been virtually handpicked by the government under the new 2023 Law for Appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners.
The Opposition Congress party had given written objections during the appointment of both in the selection committee meetings.

When Dr. Sandhu was appointed along with CEC Gyanesh Kumar on March 14, 2024, following the retirement of EC Anup Chandra Pandey and the abrupt resignation of EC Arun Goel, Congress leader Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury had given a formal dissent note in the selection committee.
Later, when Mr. Joshi was appointed on February 17, 2025 after Gyanesh Kumar was elevated to CEC, Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi raised objection in the committee meeting.
Both the Election Commissioners had reportedly flagged several key issues, including the centralisation of the Electoral Rolls.
In May this year, Mr. Joshi proposed an audit to certify that “no one except the concerned statutory authorities has any credentials to make any change in the (voter) database”.

In August, Dr. Sandhu recorded that State-level election officials were reporting that they do not have “proper and complete access” to the ERONet portal — the digital system through which the electoral rolls are maintained.

He further flagged that Election Commission Director General of IT “does not have any legal authority to restrict proper and complete access and freedom to operate as given by law to the statutory authorities”.
The two ECs also said that Form 6 — which new voters must fill to register— was altered to ask if the applicant or their parents/grandparents “exist” in the electoral roll of the last SIR.

They warned as early as May that such a statutory form cannot be changed without amending the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and Dr. Sandhu called the change “unauthorised and illegal” in August, demanding its immediate removal.

stories.headline: Mehli Mistry steps down from Tata Medical Center trust
stories.title: Mehli Mistry steps down from Tata Medical Center trust
stories.summary: Mistry, a confidante of late Ratan Tata, informed the board of the medical center he will not seek a re-election upon the end of his term on September 30
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'steps down' in title weight 40
article_sentences: Mehli Mistry has stepped down as a trustee from the board of Tata Medical Center, Kolkata.
Mistry, a confidante of late Ratan Tata, informed the board of the medical center he will not seek a re-election upon the end of his term on September 30.
Other trustees on the board include Noel Tata and his children — Neville, Leah and Maya, as well as former Defence Secretary Vijay Singh.
The Tata Medical Center run by Tata Trusts is spread across 13 acres in New Town, Kolkata.
Established in 2011 it is an integrated oncology facility with over 400 beds.
Last October, Mistry had stepped down as a trustee in three key Tata trusts after board members voted against his reappointment.
Mistry subsequently has raised issues of governance and alleged misconduct by trustees before Charity Commissioner of Maharashtra.
The matter is expected to be heard on October 15.

stories.headline: Supreme Court orders action against Mau SPs from 2023 over ‘casual approach’ in criminal case trial
stories.title: Supreme Court orders action against Mau SPs from 2023 over ‘casual approach’ in criminal case trial
stories.summary: A Bench said only two of 54 prosecution witnesses have been examined since charges were framed in a 2017 kidnapping case, calling the prosecution “absolutely slack”
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 2 independent source groups -> high confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Taking strong note of the “casual approach” of the Uttar Pradesh.

Police in a criminal case trial, the Supreme Court has directed the State Government to initiate departmental proceedings against the Superintendents of Police who have served in Mau district since 2023.

A Bench of Justices Ahsanuddin Amanullah and R. Mahadevan noted that only two of 54 prosecution witnesses had been examined in the case, lodged in 2017, despite charges being framed against six accused in March 2023.
It noted that the 14-year-old son of the petitioner was kidnapped on September 27, 2017, and that neither he nor his remains have been found to date.

“This leaves us in no doubt that the prosecution, which is accountable for producing witnesses, has been absolutely slack in its duty towards the court in the conduct of the criminal trial,” the Bench said in its order of September 21, 2026.
The Court said it was primarily the investigating agency's obligation to produce witnesses.
“We are shocked at the conduct of the prosecution in not ensuring that witnesses are produced before the court for more than three years and, as of today, only two witnesses stand examined,” it said.
The Bench noted that, pursuant to its order of August 10, 2026, the incumbent Superintendent of Police of Mau was present in court and had filed an affidavit dated August 29, 2026.

"On a query of the court as to how many witnesses have been examined since charges were framed against all six accused, lastly on March 27, 2023, the answer is that two out of 54 prosecution witnesses have been examined," the Court said.
It noted that despite the framing of charges in March 2023, the prosecuting agency had shown not even a "semblance of seriousness" in getting the trial concluded.

“Accordingly, we direct the State of Uttar Pradesh to initiate departmental proceedings against the Superintendents of Police, Mau district, Uttar Pradesh, who served from 2023 till date, for such casual approach towards a duty cast upon them, especially in matters of trial.
The same shall be initiated within two weeks from today,” the Bench said.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Orders Demolition Of 16,726 Illegal Structures In Meerut; Appoints Justice Dhulia Commission To Probe Illegal Colonies
stories.title: Supreme Court Orders Demolition Of 16,726 Illegal Structures In Meerut; Appoints Justice Dhulia Commission To Probe Illegal Colonies
stories.summary: The Court also directed the authorities to demolish every illegal structure at Meerut's Uldepur and remove the debris on a daily basis.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Court also directed the authorities to demolish every illegal structure at Meerut's Uldepur and remove the debris on a daily basis.
The Supreme Court has directed Meerut authorities to take prompt steps for the demolition of 16,726 unauthorised structures identified in Zone.
A and ordered the demolition of remaining illegal constructions in other parts of the city.

A bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice KV Viswanathan directed that occupants of the identified illegal structures first be asked to vacate and that the structures thereafter be sealed and demolished.

“We direct the authorities to proceed at the earliest to take appropriate action against all these 16,726 illegal structures in Zone-A. The first step in the process is to ask the occupants to vacate the premises and to seal all these premises, i.e., the 16,726 illegal structures.
We direct accordingly.”, the Court ordered.
Out of 16,726 structures, 12,907 comprise of residential, 874 residential-cum-non-residential, and 2945 non-residential constructions.
The Court also ordered the demolition of 138 properties where unauthorised construction had been raised in mandatory setback areas.
Of 201 such properties earlier identified, 63 had already been cleared.
The Court directed that the remaining 138 properties, with unauthorised construction in the setback areas, are also to be demolished.
During the hearing that took place in April this year, the Court was informed there were a total of 859 unauthorized structures, out of which 44 were used for commercial purposes.
These 44 illegally converted properties include six schools, six hospitals, four banquet halls, three nationalised banks, and one NBFC.

stories.headline: Sibal escalates SIR row, demands CEC’s removal and review of elections
stories.title: Sibal escalates SIR row, demands CEC’s removal and review of elections
stories.summary: Kapil Sibal has raised concerns over the Election Commission's decision-making under Gyanesh Kumar during a ten-month period. His allegations include that decisions were made unilaterally, bypassing other commissioners and statutory protocols. Sibal has called for an investigation into the electoral rolls and recent elections conducted in Bihar and West Bengal. In response, the Election Commission acknowledged concerns and proposed several corrective measures to address them.
